thread:
maya: Quick post-all-hands q: two customers pinged about what happens to latency/SLA and billing when we spill to preemptible or cross-region Dedicated. Also want the exact policy for when we evict preemptible instances. Can we summarize?
chris: Short summary: SLA holds only for Dedicated & Hosted in-region. If traffic goes to preemptible/spot or cross-region Hosted, SLA doesn't apply; we'll surface a "degradation" flag in the console. Billing: customers continue to pay for tokens consumed; burst pricing applies only for Hosted burst buckets per pricing page.
anika: On eviction: cloud provider preemption events trigger immediate eviction; we also proactively drain preemptible nodes if sustained error rate > 5% for 2m or if instance health reports degraded disk/driver. We try to avoid evicting during short spikes.
ops-bot: infra-alert: preemptible-eviction-watcher deployed v2.3 at 14:12 UTC monitoring enabled.
tom: For the customer-facing doc, can we give a simple matrix? ex: in-region Dedicated = SLA, no latency delta; nearest-region Dedicated = SLA-not-covered, typical +30-90ms; preemptible = best-effort, possible >200ms and request retries.
chris: Yup. We'll include p50/p90/p99 latency deltas for each hop in the matrix. Also we'll add estimated error-rate bump when spilling to preemptible (observed 0.2-2% higher 4xx/5xx depending on model size).
emily: Observability ask: can we tag external-fallthrough events in traces and in the console timeline so customers can see when we routed them off their pinned model/region?
anika: Good call. We'll add a "fallback.reason" tag to traces and a UI timeline entry. Example alert rule for ops that I want feedback on:
```yaml
- alert: FallbackSpillHigh
  expr: sum(rate(route_fallback_total[5m])) by (region) > 10
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "High rate of routing fallbacks in {{ $labels.region }}"
```
ryan: Ops/Oncall Q: if prewarm fails and customers are affected, who has authority to manually flip traffic to a cold-start pool or to trigger additional prewarm? Do we require SRE/Infra lead or is oncall able to?
chris: Oncall can trigger manual failover using the runbook; infra lead must approve capacity commit >2h. We'll add a quick button in the canary control panel to escalate to infra lead.
emily: For support: prepare two templates: one short customer-facing note and one technical incident note with traces/log links. Support should send short note within 30m of incident detection.
maya: Action items: chris to draft the external matrix + SLA blurb by Tue EOD; anika to add fallback.reason tracing tag and the YAML alert to the canary by Wed; emily to prepare support templates and comms copy by Wed noon; ryan to update runbook with manual-failover steps and authority matrix by end of week.
chris: I'll include measured deltas from last week's T4 burst test (p50 +45ms, p90 +120ms, p99 +280ms across EU->US fallback).
anika: Canary will include the preemptible eviction watcher and the new alert rule. I'll monitor error budgets during rollout.
ops-bot: Reminder: infra sync Thursday 09:00 UTC bcalendar invite includes links to draft PRs.
maya: Thanks all. Please mark done in the infra board when PRs are up :thumbsup:
